summary: U.S. equities pulled back on Friday after the S&P 500 hit a fresh record high of 7,798.99 on Thursday, marking the third consecutive weekly gain for the benchmark index despite deteriorating consumer sentiment. The University of Michigan's August consumer confidence reading plummeted to 51.0 from 55.2 in July, with year-ahead inflation expectations climbing to 4.3% as the U.S.-Iran conflict continues to pressure energy markets and weigh on sentiment. Meanwhile, Workday shares surged nearly 26% on reports that Silver Lake is in talks to acquire the software company, though discussions remain ongoing. In crypto markets, Bitcoin and Ethereum continued their recent weakness, trading at $62,721 and $1,873 respectively on Friday morning, as risk-off sentiment and geopolitical uncertainty in the Strait of Hormuz offset cooler inflation data that could keep the Fed on hold in September. The Fed held rates steady at 3.5%-3.75% in late July in a 9-3 vote under new Chair Kevin Warsh, with three dissenting members pushing for hikes, underscoring ongoing division about the policy path.

signals.title: Consumer Sentiment Plunges 8% in August, Inflation Fears Rise
signals.desc: University of Michigan sentiment index fell to 51.0 from 55.2 in July as inflation expectations jumped to 4.3%, pressuring equities into Friday's close.

signals.title: Workday Surges 26% on Silver Lake Takeover Talks
signals.desc: Software company Workday spiked after Reuters reported private equity firm Silver Lake is in acquisition discussions, signaling continued M&A appetite.

signals.title: S&P 500 Notches Record High at 7,799 Before Retreating
signals.desc: The benchmark index closed at an all-time high Thursday, surpassing 7,800 for the first time, before slipping 0.2% Friday on sentiment data.

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum Slide as Geopolitical Risk Weighs
signals.desc: Crypto prices declined despite softer inflation data, with Bitcoin falling to $62,721 and Ethereum to $1,873 amid ongoing Iran conflict uncertainty.

signals.title: Oil Prices Volatile Amid U.S.-Iran War and Demand Concerns
signals.desc: WTI crude fell more than 2% to $81.25 per barrel as traders balanced falling demand against supply disruptions from the Strait of Hormuz closure.

verdict: Markets consolidating at record highs but facing headwinds from deteriorating sentiment and persistent geopolitical risk as Fed policy uncertainty keeps volatility elevated.
